snippet:
Originally I come from the trend following and momentum side, and both are still an essential part of my strategy portfolio.

The interesting part: trend following 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗲𝗹𝗹 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗨𝗦 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁. At least according to a research paper I studied a while ago — and my own analyses clearly confirmed it. Trend following works much better on the 𝗔𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻 market, the 𝗖𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗻 market or the 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘃𝗶𝗮𝗻 markets.

So here is a position from my trend following model for the Australian stock market: $SXE.

The chart tells you what trend following really asks from you. The stock did nothing for almost two years, sitting around 0.70 AUD. Then a first leg up — and then 𝘁𝘄𝗲𝗹𝘃𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝘄𝗮𝘆𝘀 𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗽 between roughly 1.40 and 2.00, which is exactly the stretch where most people throw a trend position away.

My model entered at 1.887 AUD. Today: 4.84. That is +𝟭𝟱𝟲% 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, roughly 6x from where the stock was doing nothing in 2022, and +7.44% this week alone.

I did not predict any of this. The model held through the boring part because the rules said hold. For trend following it is important to cover several markets. In an ideal case Australia with small caps and large caps, Canada, Germany — and the US as an addition, although the risk-reward on the US market is not that interesting to me. Quite different for mean reversion and relative momentum strategies.

title: WSOT – World Series of Trading 2025
snippet:
WSOT – World Series of Trading 2025

Last year, I participated in the World Series of Trading with my fully systematic US Large Cap strategy portfolio. I entered without specific performance expectations—my goal was simple: to objectively assess whether my approach could stand up to the highest international trading standards.

The portfolio trades highly liquid US equities only: NASDAQ-100, S&P 500, and in two strategies the Russell 1000 universe. In total, more than 20 systematic strategies are combined—spanning long-term momentum, mean reversion, seasonal effects, and intraday models. A dedicated short strategy set was also part of the portfolio, though it played only a minor role in overall performance. All trades were executed fully automatically via professional trading software by Quant Console.

The result:
 🥈 2nd place overall, competing against experienced hedge fund managers and FX traders.
 🥇 1st place in the stock category, reinforcing my conviction that a well-designed, risk-focused systematic portfolio can compete at the highest level.

The primary objective was never short-term glory, but a robust and repeatable risk-return profile—and I’m proud that this approach proved itself under real competitive conditions.

A sincere thank you to @JoachimMo1985 , @smartestrading  and the entire WSOT team for the excellent organization and support. I’m also grateful to Adrian from @EnlightenStock , my first trading mentor, for laying the foundation years ago.

snippet:
Since the semiconductor sell-off in July my NASDAQ 100 stock portfolio had some trouble to get back in line with the market. On the one hand, I just didn't get many order fills, on the other hand due to capital limitations in the portfolio, some semi titles were not executed. In the end this is a small portfolio, yet. So same story here, the last six weeks not much happened. A great chance to check in with yourself, if you have confidence in your strategy set.

This week is the second strong week in a row. +𝟰.𝟰𝟲% 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗸, +𝟳.𝟱𝟵% 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝟭𝟬 𝗱𝗮𝘆𝘀 (USD) vs. $QQQ +0.92%. If this continues, the portfolio could print a 𝗻𝗲𝘄 𝗮𝗹𝗹-𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝗴𝗵 within the next week or two. At the same time NASDAQ100 is showing weakness. That is a precious behavior considering that this portfolio only trades NASDAQ100 stocks.

What makes me really happy here is that my 𝗻𝗲𝘄 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁-𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗺 𝗺𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘂𝗺 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀 I put live after the initial drawdown are doing exactly what they were built to do.

Current total exposure sits around 𝟱𝟬%, with a small short book active again.

Overall: +𝟯𝟰% 𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗔𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗹 when I started trading this. $QQQ is showing +𝟵.𝟭𝟳% for the same period.

snippet:

My Darwinex account has been trading live for months. That side was never the question — the portfolio does what it was built to do.

The DARWIN is a different story.

A DARWIN is not my account. It's the investable replication of it — and between the two sit execution, latency and sizing. In the early stage, that implementation had real issues: some replication metrics were simply not where I wanted them.

That's the reason I haven't published the ticker yet. Not because the underlying numbers were bad — because the replicated version wasn't yet provably the same quality I get on my own account. That gap is now closing, and the final verification is running.

𝗜𝗳 𝗜 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗾𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗜 𝗴𝗲𝘁. 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘄𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝗜 𝗱𝗼𝗻'𝘁 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘁.

𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘁.

Ticker publication is next. Stay tuned.
